content:
Sanjay Reddy: Heads-up — kicked off a small canary for q4v2-small on the chat-gen route. Lightweight traffic (~300 requests) so far, running A/B against baseline v3.
Maria Chen: Nice. Any early signal on fidelity or latency?
Sanjay Reddy: Early numbers: MRR delta ~ -1.7% (down), hallucination rate +0.4pp, latency p95 +18% (~220ms -> 260ms). Noise but worth watching.
Alex Kim: Those are close to the thresholds we discussed. Are we using the auto-fallback rules or manual for this pilot?
Sanjay Reddy: Auto-fallback enabled for this slice. Current config is conservative — min_samples=200 and composite impact scoring. Sharing the gating snippet:

```
# canary gating config (prod)
min_samples: 200
metrics:
  mrr_delta_pct: -2.0     # trigger if MRR drops more than 2%
  hallucination_delta_pp: 1.0  # trigger if hallucination increases by 1 percentage point
  latency_p95_delta_pct: 25  # trigger if p95 latency increases by 25%
composite_threshold: 2.0
rollback_action: immediate
```

Jake Torres: Can we bump min_samples to 500 for low-volume user cohorts? 200 is fine for broad slices but risky for stragglers.
Maria Chen: Agreed. Also want to include a minimum signal on content-quality slices (e.g., longform summarization) — those need fewer latency constraints and stricter hallucination limits.
Sanjay Reddy: Good call. Proposed change: min_samples -> 500 for any slice where weekly traffic < 10k. Also making composite score explicit:

```
# impact scoring (simple weighted sum)
impact = 0.6 * max(0, -mrr_delta_pct) + 0.3 * latency_p95_delta_pct + 0.1 * hallucination_delta_pp
# if impact >= composite_threshold -> trigger rollback
```

Alex Kim: That weighting seems reasonable for chat-gen. Suggest we run a quick sweep to calibrate weights on historical AB runs — we should avoid sensitivity to tiny MRR blips.
ci-bot: canary (q4v2-small) started on shard us-west-2a — 120/300 requests processed, status=running
Jake Torres: One more ask — add canary tag to traces and evaluation payloads so we can slice errors by user intent. Right now it's hard to attribute hallucinations.
Maria Chen: Also add a soft-alert to #eng-oncall when hallucinations > 0.8pp so humans can eyeball before auto-rollback.
Sanjay Reddy: Will implement: (1) adjust min_samples per slice traffic, (2) add trace tag `canary:q4v2-small`, (3) soft-alert to oncall at 0.8pp, hard-rollback at 1.0pp or impact >= 2.0. I'll post updated config after next sweep.
ci-bot: canary (q4v2-small) current stats: samples=300, mrr_delta=-1.9%, hallucination_delta=0.45pp, latency_p95_delta=19% — no rollback yet
Alex Kim: Sounds good. If numbers creep past thresholds, we prefer immediate fallback to baseline and a brief shadow run to collect failure cases.
Maria Chen: Thanks — please dump the first 50 failure traces into the S3 canary bucket for evals.
Sanjay Reddy: On it. Will follow up with a short postmortem if we end up rolling back. :thumbsup:
